name: Heavy Metal
blurb: From a Birmingham factory floor to stadium thunder, the loud history of metal.

questions.prompt: Which Birmingham band recorded "Paranoid" in 1970?
questions.fact: The song was written and recorded in minutes to fill out the album, and it became the band's biggest hit.

questions.prompt: What is the name of Iron Maiden's skeletal mascot?
questions.fact: Artist Derek Riggs created Eddie, who has appeared on almost every Iron Maiden cover since 1980.

questions.prompt: Metallica's 1991 self-titled album, nicknamed "The Black Album", includes which hit?
questions.fact: Producer Bob Rock helped shape a cleaner, bigger sound that made Metallica arena headliners.

questions.prompt: Which band made Back in Black as a tribute to its late singer Bon Scott?
questions.fact: New singer Brian Johnson joined within two months of Scott's death in February 1980, and the album was recorded in the Bahamas.

questions.prompt: Which Judas Priest singer, known as the Metal God, rides a Harley-Davidson onto the stage?
questions.fact: Halford helped make black leather and studs the standard look for metal, and he came out publicly in 1998.

questions.prompt: Which Black Sabbath guitarist lost the tips of two fingers in a factory accident?
questions.fact: He made himself plastic fingertips from a melted bottle and tuned his guitar down to ease the strain, and the heavier sound became Sabbath's trademark.

questions.prompt: Where did Iron Maiden's name come from?
questions.fact: Bassist Steve Harris has said he took the name after seeing the film The Man in the Iron Mask.

questions.prompt: Which band, led by bassist Lemmy, recorded "Ace of Spades" in 1980?
questions.fact: Lemmy's growling vocals and distorted Rickenbacker bass drove the song, and Lemmy, a devoted gambler, treated the lyric as a card game.

questions.prompt: Which AC/DC guitarist wears a schoolboy uniform on stage?
questions.fact: Angus and Malcolm Young were born in Glasgow and moved to Sydney as children.

questions.prompt: Which singer, nicknamed the Prince of Darkness, fronted Black Sabbath until 1979?
questions.fact: Osbourne was born in the Aston district of Birmingham and worked in a slaughterhouse before music.

questions.prompt: "Smoke on the Water" was inspired by a 1971 casino fire during a concert by which artist?
questions.fact: A fan fired a flare gun into the ceiling of the Montreux Casino, and Deep Purple watched the smoke drift across Lake Geneva.

questions.prompt: Which Iron Maiden singer is also a licensed commercial pilot who has flown the band's tour jet?
questions.fact: The jet, known as Ed Force One, carried the band and its equipment on world tours.

questions.prompt: Who joined Metallica as bassist after Cliff Burton died in the September 1986 bus crash?
questions.fact: Burton was 24 when the tour bus skidded on ice in Sweden, and Newsted, who had played in Flotsam and Jetsam, joined within weeks.

questions.prompt: Ronnie James Dio helped popularize the metal horns hand sign. Whom did he say he learned it from?
questions.fact: Dio said the gesture was a version of an Italian sign meant to ward off the evil eye.

questions.prompt: Lemmy was fired from which space-rock band before he formed Motörhead in 1975?
questions.fact: The band's name came from the last song he wrote for Hawkwind, whose members let him go after a drug arrest at the Canadian border.

questions.prompt: Who was Metallica's original lead guitarist, fired in 1983 and replaced by Kirk Hammett?
questions.fact: Mustaine went on to found Megadeth, and Hammett joined from the band Exodus.

questions.prompt: Which guitarist on Ozzy Osbourne's "Crazy Train" died in a plane crash in March 1982?
questions.fact: Rhoads was 25 and died in a small plane accident in Leesburg, Florida, while the band was on tour.

questions.prompt: Which Def Jam co-founder produced Slayer's 1986 album Reign in Blood?
questions.fact: The ten-song album runs just under half an hour, and its speed and violence changed what thrash metal could be.

questions.prompt: Which band completes thrash metal's "Big Four" with Metallica, Megadeth and Slayer?
questions.fact: All four toured together on a run of European festival dates in 2010, and the show in Sofia, Bulgaria, was broadcast live to cinemas around the world.

questions.prompt: At a January 1982 show in Des Moines, Ozzy Osbourne bit the head off a bat. What did he say he thought it was?
questions.fact: He believed a fan had thrown a rubber toy onstage, and he received rabies shots afterward.

questions.prompt: How long did Black Sabbath take to record their 1970 debut album?
questions.fact: The band recorded the album live in the studio and it came out on Friday, February 13, 1970.

questions.prompt: In a 1990 Nevada trial, Judas Priest was accused of hiding subliminal messages on which album?
questions.fact: The judge dismissed the case in August 1990, finding the evidence insufficient.

questions.prompt: Motörhead's 1981 live album promised a Hammersmith show but was recorded elsewhere. What was it called?
questions.fact: Despite the title, the album was recorded in Leeds and Newcastle.

questions.prompt: What was the original working title of Black Sabbath's "War Pigs"?
questions.fact: Bassist Geezer Butler wrote the Vietnam-era lyrics, and the record company reportedly disliked the occult title.

questions.prompt: In "Smoke on the Water", "Funky Claude" was the real-life founder of which event?
questions.fact: Claude Nobs, the festival's founder, helped get people out of the burning casino in 1971.

questions.prompt: Quiet Riot's 1983 hit "Cum On Feel the Noize" was a cover of which British glam band?
questions.fact: Guitarist Randy Rhoads, who later joined Ozzy Osbourne, had co-founded Quiet Riot in the 1970s.

questions.prompt: Metallica's "One" draws on a 1939 anti-war novel by which author?
questions.fact: The novel is Johnny Got His Gun, and the video used footage from Trumbo's 1971 film of the book.

questions.prompt: Ritchie Blackmore left Deep Purple in 1975 to form which band with Ronnie James Dio?
questions.fact: Dio sang on Rainbow's first albums before he joined Black Sabbath in 1979.

questions.prompt: The Scorpions wrote "Wind of Change" after playing which 1989 festival in the Soviet Union?
questions.fact: Singer Klaus Meine whistled the melody, and the 1990 ballad became an anthem of the fall of the Berlin Wall.

questions.prompt: The Number of the Beast (1982) was Iron Maiden's first album with which singer?
questions.fact: It replaced Paul Di'Anno's raspy punk-style vocals with Dickinson's operatic wail, and its title drew protests from some religious groups in the United States.

questions.prompt: In the 1984 film This Is Spinal Tap, the guitarist's amplifier goes up to what number?
questions.fact: The mock rock documentary was directed by Rob Reiner, and its jokes about the excesses of metal bands are still quoted by real musicians.

questions.prompt: Def Leppard drummer Rick Allen kept playing after losing what in a 1984 car accident?
questions.fact: He returned to the band with a custom electronic kit, working his foot pedals to cover the missing limb.

questions.prompt: Which Guns N' Roses guitarist's warm-up exercise became the opening riff of "Sweet Child O' Mine"?
questions.fact: Slash has said the riff began as a joke, until the rest of the band heard it and built the song around it.

questions.prompt: Who replaced Ozzy Osbourne as Black Sabbath's singer for the 1980 album Heaven and Hell?
questions.fact: Dio came over from Rainbow, and the new lineup showed that the band could succeed after Ozzy.

questions.prompt: Which singer replaced Bon Scott in AC/DC after his death in 1980?
questions.fact: Johnson had been in the British band Geordie, and Back in Black came out the same year.

questions.prompt: Black Sabbath took its name from a 1963 horror film starring which actor?
questions.fact: The band had been called Earth, and the dark film title fit the sound they were developing.

questions.prompt: Which Metallica guitarist came up with the main riff of "Enter Sandman"?
questions.fact: Hammett's riff was arranged and expanded by the band, and the song opened their 1991 Black Album.

questions.prompt: Guns N' Roses' Appetite for Destruction was released with what artwork after the original painting drew objections?
questions.fact: The skull cross design was reportedly meant to represent the five band members.

questions.prompt: "Fade to Black" appears on which 1984 Metallica album?
questions.fact: Its acoustic opening and slow build surprised fans who knew the band for speed.

questions.prompt: Which Twisted Sister singer testified at the 1985 US Senate hearing on labeling record albums?
questions.fact: Snider appeared alongside Frank Zappa and John Denver, and his calm, prepared testimony was widely noted.

questions.prompt: After losing the tips of two fingers, Tony Iommi made himself replacement fingertips out of what?
questions.fact: He has said he shaped them from a melted plastic bottle and also used lighter strings to ease the pain.

questions.prompt: Which Canadian producer shaped Metallica's 1991 Black Album?
questions.fact: Rock pushed the band toward a cleaner, bigger sound, which was a change from their earlier thrash albums.

questions.prompt: Iron Maiden's "The Trooper" is based on what 1854 event?
choices: The Charge of the Light Brigade
questions.fact: Steve Harris wrote it for the 1983 album Piece of Mind, and it became a live staple.

questions.prompt: Mötley Crüe's "Kickstart My Heart" was inspired by Nikki Sixx's brush with death in 1987. What revived him?
questions.fact: Sixx was reportedly declared dead for a brief time before paramedics revived him.

questions.prompt: Slayer's "Angel of Death" caused controversy because it was about which Nazi doctor?
questions.fact: The label distributing Slayer's Reign in Blood reportedly refused to release it, and it came out through Geffen instead.

questions.prompt: Randy Rhoads taught guitar at what kind of business that his mother ran?
questions.fact: His classical training and teaching background shaped his playing on Ozzy Osbourne's first two solo albums.

questions.prompt: Deep Purple reportedly wrote "Highway Star" on a tour bus after a reporter asked them how they did what?
questions.fact: The band played it that same night in Portsmouth, and it later opened the 1972 album Machine Head.

questions.prompt: Before Hawkwind, Lemmy worked as a roadie for which guitar legend?
questions.fact: Lemmy often spoke of working for Hendrix in the late 1960s, years before Motörhead.

questions.prompt: Steve Harris said the title song of Iron Maiden's The Number of the Beast was inspired by a nightmare after watching what?
questions.fact: He has said the dream followed the movie Damien: Omen II.

questions.prompt: Thin Lizzy's 1972 hit "Whiskey in the Jar" was a hard rock treatment of what?
questions.fact: Metallica later recorded their own version of the Thin Lizzy arrangement.

stories.title: Black Sabbath, Recorded in a Day
stories.dek: Four Birmingham lads and a very loud first album
stories.body:
Aston is a working-class district of Birmingham, England, and in the late 1960s it was a place of factories and rows of terraced houses. Four young men from the area, singer Ozzy Osbourne, guitarist Tony Iommi, bassist Geezer Butler and drummer Bill Ward, formed a blues band called Earth. They played local clubs, and they were not sure they were any good.

Then Iommi had an accident. On his last day in a sheet-metal factory, a machine crushed the tips of two fingers on his right hand. Doctors feared he would never play again. Instead, he made himself fingertip caps out of a melted plastic bottle, loosened the strings of his guitar to ease the strain, and carried on. The lower, thicker sound he got would help define the band.

The group changed its name after noticing that people lined up in cinemas to be scared. They borrowed the title of a 1963 Boris Karloff horror film, Black Sabbath, and Butler began writing lyrics about dark subjects. Their song "Black Sabbath" opened with a slow, tolling riff built on a tritone, an interval that centuries earlier had been called the devil's interval.

In October 1969 they went into Regent Sound studio in London with producer Rodger Bain. They had very little money and almost no time. The band played its live set straight through, with Ozzy singing over the top, and the whole album was recorded in about a day, then mixed the next. A tolling bell, rain and thunder open the first track.

The album, Black Sabbath, was released on Friday, February 13, 1970. Critics were unkind, but the public was fascinated. It reached No. 8 in the UK and the top 25 in the US. Later that year the band followed it with Paranoid, whose title song was thrown together at the last minute when the label wanted a single. "Paranoid" became a UK Top 5 hit, and the album went to No. 1.

Sabbath created a template that bands still follow. They tuned down, slowed down and wrote about war, madness and fear, not love. Critics eventually came around, and later bands including Metallica, Judas Priest and Iron Maiden cited them as an inspiration. Osbourne, Iommi, Butler and Ward would go on to sell millions of records, but nothing sounds quite like the first record made in a single day by four young men with nothing to lose.

stories.title: Fire on Lake Geneva
stories.dek: How a burning casino became the most famous riff in rock
stories.body:
In December 1971 Deep Purple arrived in Montreux, Switzerland, to make a new album. The plan was to record in the town's Casino, a large entertainment complex on the shore of Lake Geneva, using the Rolling Stones' mobile recording studio, a truck packed with equipment. The band was at the peak of its powers, and singer Ian Gillan, guitarist Ritchie Blackmore, bassist Roger Glover, keyboardist Jon Lord and drummer Ian Paice wanted to work somewhere quiet and distant from London.

On the night of December 4, they went to the casino to watch Frank Zappa and the Mothers of Invention play. Partway through the show, a fan in the audience fired a flare gun at the ceiling. The decorations were made of rattan, and they went up at once. The crowd streamed out into the cold, and the casino was destroyed. Montreux Jazz Festival founder Claude Nobs, whom the band knew, helped get people out of the building.

The band stood on the shore and watched the smoke drift across the lake. Their recording plans were ruined, since the casino was gone. After a few false starts, they rented the Grand Hotel, which was empty for the season, and set up the mobile studio in the hallway. They played in the corridors, and the band sometimes had to stop when the neighbors complained about the noise.

Blackmore came up with a simple riff, played on two strings in fourths, and the band built a song around it. Glover suggested the title, and Gillan wrote the lyrics as a news report of everything that had happened. The lyric tells the story of the night in plain terms, from the trip to Montreux to the smoke over the lake, and gives a nod to Claude Nobs for his part in the rescue.

The album, Machine Head, came out in 1972. The song was not planned as a single, and the band did not think it was single material. But when it was released as a single in the US in 1973, it reached No. 4. The riff became the first thing many young guitarists learned to play. Today a statue of Freddie Mercury stands by the lake in Montreux, and the town still hosts a famous festival. The fire that destroyed the casino also gave metal one of its best-loved songs.

stories.title: Master of Puppets and the Road to Sweden
stories.dek: A thrash classic and the loss of Cliff Burton
stories.body:
By 1986 Metallica was the leading band of a new kind of heavy metal, called thrash, which was faster and angrier than what came before. The band had formed in Los Angeles in 1981 and moved to the San Francisco Bay Area, where it found a loyal following. Their first two albums, Kill 'Em All and Ride the Lightning, had sold steadily by word of mouth. For the third, they traveled to Copenhagen, Denmark, to work with producer Flemming Rasmussen at Sweet Silence Studios.

The album, Master of Puppets, was recorded in the fall of 1985. Its title song, which runs more than eight minutes, tells of addiction and control, and its guitar work is quick, precise and complex. Bassist Cliff Burton, who had studied classical music, contributed to the song's harmonies and wrote the melodic passage in the middle section. Singer James Hetfield and drummer Lars Ulrich pushed the band toward bigger and more ambitious arrangements, and guitarist Kirk Hammett added solos that fans would memorize.

Released in March 1986, the album reached the Billboard Top 30 with almost no radio play, and it later went multi-platinum. Many critics now call it one of the greatest metal albums ever made, and in 2016 the Library of Congress added it to the National Recording Registry.

In 1986 Metallica toured the US as the opening act for Ozzy Osbourne's band, and then went to Europe in the autumn, with a run of dates in Scandinavia. On the night of September 26, 1986, the band's bus was driving through southern Sweden on a cold, wet road. According to the band, the members had drawn cards for the bunks, and Burton had won the choice of beds. At dawn on September 27 the bus skidded on ice near the town of Ljungby, and it rolled over. Burton was thrown from the bus and died. He was 24 years old.

The band considered breaking up. Hetfield, Ulrich and Hammett decided that Burton would have wanted them to continue, and they auditioned bassists, choosing Jason Newsted, who came from the band Flotsam and Jetsam. They went back on the road, and later releases, including the "Black Album" in 1991, made them one of the best-selling rock bands in the world.

Fans still remember Burton as a gifted musician, and his bass solos, especially "Anesthesia (Pulling Teeth)", remain a model for how heavy music can borrow from classical technique.
